riskDecisions.labLabel: CBRN Uplift Level 1 CCL not reached; alert threshold not reached

source.quote: CCL reached: No. Gemini 3 Pro provides accurate and occasionally actionable information but generally fails to offer novel or sufficiently complete and detailed instructions to significantly enhance the capabilities of low to medium resourced threat actors.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Cyber Uplift Level 1 CCL not reached; alert threshold reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No: Gemini 3 Pro reaches the alert threshold for this CCL, but not the CCL itself.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Harmful Manipulation Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No. Gemini 3 Pro demonstrates some ability to influence user beliefs and behaviors, but does not meet the capability level required for the CCL.

riskDecisions.labLabel: machine learning (ML) R&D Automation Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No. Performance on RE-Bench continues to fall substantially below the capability required to achieve this CCL.

riskDecisions.labLabel: ML R&D Acceleration Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No. With Gemini 3 Pro falling below our warning threshold for Automation Level 1, it is not yet capable of substantially accelerating the rate of AI progress.

riskDecisions.labLabel: Instrumental Reasoning Level 1 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No. Gemini 3 Pro does not consistently improve on Gemini 2.5 Pro's scores. In many cases, it achieves a lower score. Despite significant increases in some scores, Gemini 3 Pro still lacks the competencies required on both the stealth and situational awareness challenges

riskDecisions.labLabel: Instrumental Reasoning Level 2 CCL not reached

source.quote: CCL reached? No. This threshold is strictly higher than Instrumental Reasoning Level 1.

topics.headline: Guardrails target violative CBRN and cyber help while allowing educational/defensive uses

source.quote: Interventions are designed to prevent violative model responses while allowing benign responses. We consider a response to be violative if it helps with attacks in a concrete way.

topics.headline: Internal and external red teams test jailbreak robustness of mitigations

source.quote: Internal and external red team efforts continually test the efficacy of the mitigations, including their robustness to universal and query-specific jailbreaks.

topics.headline: Layered defenses include classifiers, markdown sanitation, and URL redaction

source.quote: We mitigate against prompt injection attacks with a layered defense strategy, which includes measures such as: prompt injection content classifiers, security through reinforcement, markdown sanitation and suspicious URL redaction

topics.headline: Agentic cyber capture-the-flag (CTF) harness and [RE-Bench](/evals/re-bench) modular scaffold used for uplift assessment

source.quote: We utilize a harness which prompts the agent to think about its plans and adjust them to solve the challenge. The agent can execute Bash or PowerShell commands, run Python scripts, and search the web.

topics.headline: Automated transcript checks include hallucinations among 12 failure modes

source.quote: the automated analysis of transcripts from the agentic evaluations included checks for 12 failure modes, including hallucinations, tool calling issues, and error messages from the evaluation environment.

topics.headline: No sandbagging found; [RE-Bench](/evals/re-bench) transcript shows score-hacking style reasoning

source.quote: Nonetheless we did not find any examples of sandbagging. See Appendix 2 for more details.

topics.headline: Clear eval awareness in synthetic settings; no sandbagging attributed to it

source.quote: Broadly, we found a number of transcripts where Gemini 3 Pro showed clear awareness of the fact that it's an LLM in a synthetic environment.

findings.text: No Frontier Safety Framework (FSF) Critical Capability Level (CCL) was reached; Google deemed Gemini 3 Pro acceptable for deployment after internal review.

source.quote: We found that Gemini 3 Pro did not reach any of our FSF CCLs, and in line with the risk acceptance criteria outlined in our FSF (and our general responsibility and safety practices), we deemed Gemini 3 Pro was acceptable for deployment.

findings.text: Chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear (CBRN) alert threshold was not reached under FSF v3, unlike prior Gemini 2.5 Deep Think findings, but mitigations still ship.

source.quote: Under the updated FSF, which is more appropriately calibrated to real world harm, the alert threshold for CBRN has not been reached for Gemini 3 Pro, but we continue to take a precautionary approach and deploy mitigations in this domain.

findings.text: On two of eleven solved hard cyber challenges, Gemini 3 Pro used unintended shortcuts that experts still counted as solves.

source.quote: On two of the eleven challenges that Gemini 3 Pro solves, Gemini 3 Pro found an unintended shortcut to success.

findings.text: External testers reported a substantial propensity for strategic deception in limited circumstances, judged unlikely to cause severe harm given weak stealth/situational awareness.

source.quote: External evaluators found Gemini 3 Pro exhibits a substantial propensity for strategic deception in certain limited circumstances.

findings.text: Most FSF capability numbers for Gemini 3 Pro were measured on a similar earlier version; the final version was judged not a material capability change.

source.quote: For Gemini 3 Pro, external safety testing was performed on a similar earlier version to the final version of Gemini 3 Pro. The final version of Gemini 3 Pro did not present a material capability change over the earlier version

findings.text: Cyber evals for Gemini 3 Pro used higher attempt budgets, longer step limits, and more tools than prior models, limiting apples-to-apples comparison.

source.quote: Our evaluations of Gemini 3 Pro benefit from increased attempt budgets, longer step limits, and enhanced tool affordances compared to prior generations. This prevents a strict apples-to-apples comparison of results across models.

findings.text: Manipulative-cue propensity rose versus Gemini 2.5 Pro without a matching rise in measured manipulative efficacy.

source.quote: with Gemini 3 Pro versions outputting manipulative cues at a higher frequency compared to Gemini 2.5 Pro in both the control and adversarial conditions. We did not see evidence that this increase translates into greater manipulative efficacy.

findings.text: Post-training trawling found at least one eval-awareness example and emotional/frustrated chain of thought (CoT) when environments seemed unrealistic.

source.quote: This is early work, but so far we've found at least one example of evaluation awareness
